how: Repeated calls recruit helpers to finish one figure and start the next rather than assuming an already assembled workforce.
A participant identifies a figure they started and credits the helpers who joined its construction.
Proposals enlarge the display with additional characters and a subreddit logo.
A coordinate-bearing report makes partial completion visible to prospective helpers.
Coordinates, dimensions, and ordered rows translate intended images into executable placement instructions.

statement: routing helpers to detailed external discussion
how: Helpers are routed to an external discussion venue for detailed coordination whose internal decisions are not visible.
Routing helpers to detailed discussion supplements coordinate circulation without showing that the discussion settled the design.
Instruction circulation does not establish one agreed standard when background dimensions differ between surviving specifications.
Visible repair pressure and external coordination provide no evidence deciding whether placers used scripts or spare accounts.
A bare promise to maintain the finished image asks nothing in return.
One room with procedural decisions and unseen discussion cannot test the model's aggregate frequency of decided organization.
A local reading of undecided order must distinguish moderators' chosen discussion procedures from unobserved authority over placing.
Completion creates maintenance demands and ongoing repairs delay the next proposed build.
Repair priorities can deliberately withhold attention from tampering while builders finish another figure.
A participant attributes a missing feature tentatively to their own attempted improvement rather than confidently blaming an enemy.
Participants investigate a damaged name through a vandalism question and an account of repeated pixel removal.
An individual judges encroachment too fast and considers abandoning the attempt before reversing that judgment.
Inferring abandonment or relocation requires a sustained room decision because an individual's withdrawal can reverse within the same edited report.
Participants negotiate retention of reduced figures within a neighbour's expanding design.
An accepted agreement may reflect constrained accommodation to an expanding neighbour rather than equal choice over its terms.
An announced compromise still requires redirecting repair work when a reply reports rebuilding the figures that the agreed icon replaces.
A larger neighbour's template conditions the survival of reduced guest artwork on integration within its design.
Participants accept a smaller integrated version as a survival plan rather than documenting a completed move to a new location.
Builders are instructed to leave neighbouring creations intact and respect surrounding sprites.
A conditional offer exchanges help building one figure for repairing another group's artwork.
A mutual-watch proposal and an explicit alliance report support cooperation among neighbouring groups without independent observation of their compliance.
A self-identified messenger carries another group's request to help build final icons.
A rebuilding report answers a compromise instruction without explicitly challenging who can commit the room to the agreement.
Inferring a mandate dispute from negotiation requires explicit authority claims because ongoing rebuilding can reflect a different plan or incomplete knowledge.
Fictional characters supply familiar language for joking about damage to the shared canvas.
Treating a name as inherited identity requires evidence it predates the event rather than arising affectionately from the event's damage.
The renewed defense call names a canvas adversary without establishing a quarrel carried over from before the event.
Canvas resistance and fandom language do not establish that a pre-existing tie named the rival in the attack turn.
Explicit April Fools jokes and a reported takeover run beside the practical canvas work.
Moderators gather crowded suggestions into a megathread and specify its ordering and visibility rules.
Participants celebrate surviving work and thank those who helped with a personally started figure.
Retrospective participation claims value small contributions and effort sustained because the event was temporary.
The retrospective records missing features and failed repairs while valuing figures that survived.
A post-close invitation carries the character build to a successor canvas with coordinates and a starting instruction.
A crossover request expresses a possible future tie without demonstrating its implementation.
Participants adopt an accidental damaged name affectionately rather than requiring a restored image before carrying the event forward.
Mourning a defect and loving the damaged name do not establish a contest over cleaned copies or the historical account.
A builder reports overwriting neighbouring artwork to establish a border.
Defense talk names the advancing taskbar as an opponent and calls for a collective stand.
Recruitment and retrospective participation are visible but these concepts cannot attribute specific building or state reports to particular calls.
Retrospective starter credit and an appeal for help do not establish a traced starter-to-recruitment sequence for one build.
The same report explicitly joins a completed figure to continuing vandalism and a need for maintainers.
A proposal changes the figures' background to match the advancing taskbar expressly to improve their chances of not being overwritten.
Restraint instructions do not identify the reported border or a negotiated settlement as the reason for sparing other creations.
Repair strain is explicit but hidden coordination and missing placement-tool evidence prevent testing a turn to automation.
Celebration explicitly names the figure's having been made and survived as its object.
Interpreting celebration as preceding fate-recording must allow both to occur in the same gratitude or mourning passage.
The new-canvas invitation and ended-area account do not identify recording or remembering as the cause of continuation.
Specific instructions and disagreement over repair targets do not show a template settling design talk.
The bare maintenance commitment replies to a completion post rather than supplying a coded call-and-acceptance pair that tests the theorised mechanism.
A defense appeal establishes help-seeking under pressure but a separate alliance report cannot verify fulfilment of every request.
The repair bargain and alliance report do not state that earlier border negotiation opened their channel of exchange.
A recruitment appeal and an independent report of covering a neighbour do not establish that recruitment caused the overwrite.
The restraint instruction does not explicitly answer the separate report of covering neighbouring artwork.
The covering report and reduced-design negotiation do not explicitly connect the former to the latter.
The taskbar defense rhetoric does not explicitly arise from the separate covering of neighbouring artwork.
A participant proposes mutual artwork watching while both groups face trolls, and a later statement reports reciprocal alliance maintenance.
The moderator expressly gives crowding by suggestions as the reason to gather them in one thread.

statement: explaining the finished event to people who missed it
how: Post-event questions receive explanations of the canvas and the room's contributions rather than instructions for joining ongoing placement.
An explanation after closure makes the event legible but cannot be treated as increasing the original canvas's placing workforce.
Completing one figure explicitly becomes the premise for renewed recruitment to the next rather than ending mobilization after a single start.
